answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit bids or vote. A signal from a new account then carries weight only in proportion to its locked stake and its record of fulfilled tasks; copying credentials does not multiply either. At a summit, participants can challenge suspicious clusters, with proven collusion forfeiting stake. The attacker must therefore acquire and immobilize real capital for every identity, risking losses if the identities are exposed, rather than generating cheap accounts with a cipher or script.
